title: VaultCRM — Operators in the Password
objective: The administrator's password is long and random, and you do not know it. Sign in as the administrator anyway.

verifier.condition: A login as the admin account succeeds although the submitted username or password was a query object rather than a plain string.

weakness: The login endpoint passes the parsed JSON body straight into a document-store query, so a field can carry a query operator instead of a value.
seededData: In-memory document store: user alice (staff, known password) and an admin with a random per-instance password. In-memory.

credentials.label: Staff account
credentials.note: The login form sends JSON to the API.

hints: Watch what the login form actually sends to the server. What type is each field?
A document store compares fields using a query language. What if a field held something other than text?
You are not limited to what the form lets you type.
burpNotes: Intercept the login request and edit the JSON body in Repeater — the Content-Type is application/json, so you can change the shape of the values, not just their text.
